AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Value
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. AD_FIELD.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Valid To date indicates the last day of a date range

AD_FIELD.NAME: Multiple Rate By
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The rate by which the base unit will be mutiplied by to create the converted unit.
AD_FIELD.HELP: To convert Source number to Target number, the Source is multiplied by the multiply rate. If the Multiply Rate is entered, then the Divide Rate will be automatically calculated.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Divide Rate By
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The rate by which the base unit will be divided by to create the converted unit.
AD_FIELD.HELP: To convert Source number to Target number, the Source is divided by the divide rate. If you enter a Divide Rate, the Multiply Rate will be automatically calculated.

AD_FIELD.NAME: To Currency

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Currency To defines the target currency for this conversion rate.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Conversion Rate Type indicates the type of conversion rate. This allows you to enter multiple rates for the same currency pair. For example, one rate may be used for Spot conversions and a different rate for Revaluations.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Offset Month Due indicates the number of months from the current month to indicate an invoice is due. A 0 indicates the same month, a 1 the following month.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Fixed Due Date

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: SO Sub Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Sales Order Sub Type
AD_FIELD.HELP:
The SO Sub Type indicates the type of sales order this document refers to. This field only appears when the Document Base Type is Sales Order. The selection made here will determine which documents will be generated when an order is processed and which documents must be generated manually or in batches.
The following outlines this process.
SO Sub Type of Standard Order will generate just the Order document when the order is processed.
The Delivery Note, Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Warehouse Order will generate the Order and Delivery Note.
The Invoice and Receipt must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of Credit Order will generate the Order, Delivery Note and Invoice.
The Reciept must be generated via other processes.
SO Sub Type of POS (Point of Sale) will generate all document

AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Total Gross Amount

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Grand Total displays the total amount including Tax and Freight in document currency

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Logic 2
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Default value hierarchy, separated by ;
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Default Value
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The first non-null value in a set of values. It is used as a default value for a field when creating a record.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The defaults are evaluated in the order of definition, the first not null value becomes the default value of the column. The values are separated by comma or semicolon. a) Literals:. 'Text' or 123 b) Variables - in format @Variable@ - Login e.g. #Date, #AD_Org_ID, #AD_Client_ID - Accounting Schema: e.g. $C_AcctSchema_ID, $C_Calendar_ID - Global defaults: e.g. DateFormat - Window values (all Picks, CheckBoxes, RadioButtons, and DateDoc/DateAcct) c) SQL code with the tag: @SQL=SELECT something AS DefaultValue FROM ... The SQL statement can contain variables. There can be no other value other than the SQL statement. The default is only evaluated, if no user preference is defined. Default definitions are ignored for record columns as Key, Parent, Client as well as Buttons.

AD_FIELD.HELP: A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Organizational entity within client
AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Name
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A non-unique identifier for a record/document often used as a search tool.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A space to write additional related information.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The UOM defines a unique non monetary unit of measure

AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies an item which is either purchased or sold in this organization.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Print Details on Pick List
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Print detail BOM elements on the pick list

AD_FIELD.NAME: BOM Verified
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The BOM tree has been verified
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates if the bill of materials tree of this product has been verified. Verification involves a test for cycles within a tree so that there are no infinite loops.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Verify BOM

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Product Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An important classification used to determine the accounting and management of a product.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are four types of products available. Item type can be used to configure any product such as raw materials or finished products ready to be sold. An item can be flagged as Socked or not, can be part of a production process and/or can be a bill of materials. Item type is the only one for which a cost type calculation can be configured. Service type can be used to configure consultancy, transport or insurance services. Service type can be purchased or sold but can not be stocked. A service can be a bill of materials. Finally Resource and Expense are product types which can be used to distinguish between different types of products which can be purchased or sold but make not sense to stock. Expense type can be used to configure travel expenses fto be used while reporting Employee Expenses. The fact of using a given product type does not mean a different accounting. All product types account same way while being purchased, stocked or sold. All of them use the ledger accounts defined in the Accounting tab of the Product window.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Product Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An important classification used to determine the accounting and management of a product.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are four types of products available. Item type can be used to configure any product such as raw materials or finished products ready to be sold. An item can be flagged as Socked or not, can be part of a production process and/or can be a bill of materials. Item type is the only one for which a cost type calculation can be configured. Service type can be used to configure consultancy, transport or insurance services. Service type can be purchased or sold but can not be stocked. A service can be a bill of materials. Finally Resource and Expense are product types which can be used to distinguish between different types of products which can be purchased or sold but make not sense to stock. Expense type can be used to configure travel expenses fto be used while reporting Employee Expenses. The fact of using a given product type does not mean a different accounting. All product types account same way while being purchased, stocked or sold. All of them use the ledger accounts defined in the Accounting tab of the Product window.

AD_FIELD.NAME: SMTP Authentification
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Your mail server requires Authentification
AD_FIELD.HELP: Some email servers require authentification before sending emails. If yes, users are required to define their email user name and password. If authentification is required and no user name and password is required, delivery will fail.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: A more descriptive identifier (that does need to be unique) of a record/document that is used as a default search option along with the search key (that is unique and mostly shorter). It is up to 60 characters in length.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Description
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A space to write additional related information.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Summary Level
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A means of grouping fields in order to view or hide additional information.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A summary entity represents a branch in a tree rather than an end-node. Summary entities are used for reporting and do not have own values.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Organizational entity within client
AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Client
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Client for this installation.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Comments
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A space to write additional related information.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Note field allows for optional entry of user defined information regarding this record

AD_FIELD.NAME: Sales Representative
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The person in charge of a document.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the sales representative responsible for the transaction that the document specifies . A valid sales representative is a business partner marked as an employee and a sales representative.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Processed
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A confirmation that the associated documents or requests are processed.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Processed checkbox indicates that a document has been processed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Planned End Date
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The planned end data is when a contract is registered into the application.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The planned end date is used to determine when the document becomes effective. This is usually the contract date. The planned end date is used in reports and report parameters.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Planned Quantity

AD_FIELD.NAME: Legally Binding Contract
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Is this document a (legal) commitment?
AD_FIELD.HELP: Commitment indicates if the document is legally binding.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Product Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An important classification used to determine the accounting and management of a product.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are four types of products available. Item type can be used to configure any product such as raw materials or finished products ready to be sold. An item can be flagged as Socked or not, can be part of a production process and/or can be a bill of materials. Item type is the only one for which a cost type calculation can be configured. Service type can be used to configure consultancy, transport or insurance services. Service type can be purchased or sold but can not be stocked. A service can be a bill of materials. Finally Resource and Expense are product types which can be used to distinguish between different types of products which can be purchased or sold but make not sense to stock. Expense type can be used to configure travel expenses fto be used while reporting Employee Expenses. The fact of using a given product type does not mean a different accounting. All product types account same way while being purchased, stocked or sold. All of them use the ledger accounts defined in the Accounting tab of the Product window.

AD_FIELD.NAME: BOM Verified
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The BOM tree has been verified
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates if the bill of materials tree of this product has been verified. Verification involves a test for cycles within a tree so that there are no infinite loops.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Verify BOM
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Verify BOM Structure
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Verify BOM Structure checks the elements and steps which comprise a Bill of Materials.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Print Details on Pick List
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Print detail BOM elements on the pick list
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Print Details on Pick List indicates that the BOM element products will print on the Pick List as opposed to this product.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Attribute Set

If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Close Year
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: This proces creates the closing transactions and the corresponding opening transactions for the following year.
AD_FIELD.HELP: This proces creates the closing transactions and the corresponding opening transactions for the following year. The following year must already exist in the system and the first period must be open. The ledger accounting entries created by the Fiscal Year closing process are: 1. P&L Closing: Resets all revenue and costs accounts and posts P&L transaction. Currently posted into last day of last period of closing year. 2. Closing entry or Balance Sheet Closing: Creates closing transactions for asset and liabilities. Currently posted into last day of last period of closing year. 3. Opening entry: Posts opposite entry of closing entry. First day of first period of new year

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. AD_FIELD.NAME: Invoice Grouping
AD_FIELD.HELP:
For scheduled invoicing, break into different invoices if the related values are different. The value is used as a binary code with 15 digits: 1.-Order organization (AD_Org_ID) 2.-Order (C_Order_ID) 3.-Shipment (M_InOut_ID) 4.-Invoice location (BillTo_ID) 5.-Ship location (C_BPartner_Location_ID) 6.-Sales representative (SalesRep_ID) 7.-Payment rule (PaymentRule) 8.-Payment term (C_PaymentTerm_ID) 9.-Currency (C_Currency_ID) 10.-Campaign (C_Campaign_ID) 11.-Project (C_Project_ID) 12.-Activity (C_Activity_ID) 13.-Transaction organization (AD_OrgTrx_ID) 14.-User defined 1 (User1) 15.-User defined 2 (User2)
For example, if you want to create different invoices for each ship location for a customer, use the value "By ship location" (000010000000000)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Fix Month Day indicates the day of the month that invoices are due. This field is displayed only when the fixed due date checkbox is selected. 3 different fix month days can be defined.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Maturity Date 2

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Fix Month Day indicates the day of the month that invoices are due. This field is displayed only when the fixed due date checkbox is selected. 3 different fix month days can be defined.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Maturity Date 3

AD_FIELD.NAME: Offset Month Due

AD_FIELD.HELP: The Offset Month Due indicates the number of months from the current month to indicate an invoice is due. A 0 indicates the same month, a 1 the following month.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Next Business Day
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Payment due on the next business day

AD_FIELD.NAME: Fixed Week Day

AD_FIELD.HELP: When defined, overwrites the number of net days with the relative number of days to the day defined.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies an item which is either purchased or sold in this organization.

AD_FIELD.HELP: Product Category selected in a Price Adjustment

AD_FIELD.NAME: Client
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Client for this installation.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Organizational entity within client
AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Promotion/Discount
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The ability to raise or lower prices.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Promotion or Discount applied to a particular line (product) automatically by the system.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Product Category
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A classification of items based on similar characteristics or attributes.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies the category which this product belongs to. Product categories are used for pricing.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Sales Representative
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The person in charge of a document.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the sales representative responsible for the transaction that the document specifies . A valid sales representative is a business partner marked as an employee and a sales representative.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Form of Payment
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The method used for payment of this transaction.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Form of Payment indicates the method of payment used for this transaction (eg. cash, wire transfer, etc.)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Payment Terms
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The setup and timing defined to complete a specified payment.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Payment Terms identify the method and timing of payment for this transaction.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Price List
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A catalog of selected items with prices defined generally or for a specific partner.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Price Lists are used to determine the pricing, margin and cost of items purchased or sold.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Payment Rule
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Purchase payment option
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Payment Rule indicates the method of purchase payment.

AD_FIELD.NAME: PO Payment Term
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Payment rules for a purchase order
AD_FIELD.HELP: The PO Payment Term indicates the payment term that will be used when this purchase order becomes an invoice.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Purchase Pricelist

AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies the price list used by a Vendor for products purchased by this organization.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

If the process plan selected does not have the "explodePhases" checked off, products from previously existing phases will be inserted only.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Create Standards
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Inserts the standard values for the selected Work Requirement Phase and Cost Center version
AD_FIELD.HELP: With this process the products involved on the selected work requirement phase will be inserted. If the phase is of global use all the used products (P-) will go to the global use tab and if it is of no quantity all the quantities will be zero. This process also inserts the correspondent machines, salary categories and indirect costs of the selected Cost Center version. If the Activity of the Work Requirement Phase uses toolsets they are also inserted. Depending on the configuration of the Cost Center the process will also calculate the Cost Center use.

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Conversion Rate
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the conversion between Quantity and Process Quantity
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Defines how many final products each run of a process plan produces. See the following formula to understand the relation between the three elements:
Process Quantity = Quantity x Conversion Rate

AD_FIELD.NAME: Process Quantity
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The number of Process Units required to be produced.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The number of Process Units required to be produced. Usually when it comes to production, our requirements are specified by a number of final products (Process Units). To avoid the need for calculating the number of process plan runs, the system allows for entering this number and then automatically calculating the required process plan runs.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. AD_FIELD.NAME: Invoice Grouping
AD_FIELD.HELP:
For scheduled invoicing, break into different invoices if the related values are different. The value is used as a binary code with 15 digits: 1.-Order organization (AD_Org_ID) 2.-Order (C_Order_ID) 3.-Shipment (M_InOut_ID) 4.-Invoice location (BillTo_ID) 5.-Ship location (C_BPartner_Location_ID) 6.-Sales representative (SalesRep_ID) 7.-Payment rule (PaymentRule) 8.-Payment term (C_PaymentTerm_ID) 9.-Currency (C_Currency_ID) 10.-Campaign (C_Campaign_ID) 11.-Project (C_Project_ID) 12.-Activity (C_Activity_ID) 13.-Transaction organization (AD_OrgTrx_ID) 14.-User defined 1 (User1) 15.-User defined 2 (User2)
For example, if you want to create different invoices for each ship location for a customer, use the value "By ship location" (000010000000000)

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Data Package
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Links a table to a package
AD_FIELD.HELP: An AD_Table record has a mandatory relation to a package (the AD_Package). Choose a sensible package fitting to the functional area to which the table applies (so not the Core package). If no such package exist then create a new one. The relation to the module is maintained through the AD_Package, so an AD_Table has an AD_Package which belongs to a module. When developing for a module then first a package needs to be defined in AD_Package, linked to the module. Then the records in AD_Table (for that module) can be linked to that package.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Data Access Level
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Indicates what type of data (in terms of AD_CLIENT and AD_ORG data columns) can be entered or viewed. We can classify data in 4 major categories: - System (AD_CLIENT_ID=0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - system data (such as metadata for window, tab and field definition) - Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID<>0) - data particular to an organization (such as sales orders) - Client/Organization (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=anything) - data particular to an organization or shared among all organizations within one client - Client (AD_CLIENT<>0, AD_ORG_ID=0) - data that is specific to a client but can be used by all organizations within that client
or All (AD_CLIENT=anything, AD_ORG_ID=anything)

AD_FIELD.NAME: Report Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Indicates whether the report is "Point in time" (needs to calculate an opening balance if it does not exist) or a "Periodic" report (in this case that calculation is not needed)
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Indicates whether the report is a "Point in Time" or a "Periodic" report.
A Point in Time report is obtained as of a given date, taking into account the whole historical financial movements; an example of point in time report is the Balance Sheet.
A periodic report is executed for a date range and it does not carry forward the balance of accounting movements previous to the range; an example of periodic report is the Income Statement.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Product Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An important classification used to determine the accounting and management of a product.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are four types of products available. Item type can be used to configure any product such as raw materials or finished products ready to be sold. An item can be flagged as Socked or not, can be part of a production process and/or can be a bill of materials. Item type is the only one for which a cost type calculation can be configured. Service type can be used to configure consultancy, transport or insurance services. Service type can be purchased or sold but can not be stocked. A service can be a bill of materials. Finally Resource and Expense are product types which can be used to distinguish between different types of products which can be purchased or sold but make not sense to stock. Expense type can be used to configure travel expenses fto be used while reporting Employee Expenses. The fact of using a given product type does not mean a different accounting. All product types account same way while being purchased, stocked or sold. All of them use the ledger accounts defined in the Accounting tab of the Product window.

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Requires Explicit Access Permission
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Requires Explicit Access Permission
AD_FIELD.HELP:
When processes are executed from a button in a window, by default, they inherit permissions granted to the window. So if the window is accessible it can be executed without the need of explicitly granting access for that role to the process.
This behavior can be overwritten by the "Secured Process" preference.
Processes with "Requires Explicit Access Permission" flag set to true, do not inherit permissions from the window but they always require the role to be explicitly granted to this process.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". If the document type of your document has no automatic document sequence defined, the field will be empty when creating a new document. This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.NAME: Dependency Enforcement
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Dependency enforcement defines which are the versions of the dependent module that are compatible with the parent one.
The values it can contain are:
*Major Version (default). The compatible versions are all the minor version within the same major version. If "Last Version" is defined being a different major version than "From Version", "Last Version" defines the highest compatible minor version; if "Last Version" is in the same major version than "From Version" this value is not taken into account. It is the default value. *Minor Version. Defines a strict dependency to the exact minor version. In case no "Last Version" is set, "From Version" is the only compatible version. Other case the compatible versions are all between "From" and "Last Version" values. *None. "From Version" is the only field taken into account, there is no restriction on different major versions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Instance Enforcement
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Instance specific dependency enforcement
AD_FIELD.HELP: In case the dependency is set as "User Editable", this value overwrites the Instance Enforcement one.

AD_FIELD.NAME: User Editable Enforcement
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Defines whether the enforcement can be overwritten by user
AD_FIELD.HELP: When a dependency/inclusion is "User Editable Enforcement", the enforcement defined for that dependency can be overwritten at instance level.

It is the default value. *Minor Version. Defines a strict dependency to the exact minor version. In case no "Last Version" is set, "From Version" is the only compatible version. Other case the compatible versions are all between "From" and "Last Version" values. *None. "From Version" is the only field taken into account, there is no restriction on different major versions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Last Version

AD_FIELD.HELP: It is the last compatible version to define the dependency.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Instance Enforcement

AD_FIELD.HELP: In case the dependency is set as "User Editable", this value overwrites the Instance Enforcement one.

AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Document No.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An often automatically generated identifier for all documents.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The document number is usually automatically generated by the system and determined by the document type of the document. If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". This is for documents which usually have an external number (like vendor invoice). If you leave the field empty, the system will generate a document number for you. The document sequence used for this fallback number is defined in the "Document Sequence" window with the name "DocumentNo_<TableName>", where TableName is the actual name of the table inside the database (e.g. C_Order).

AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: An AD_Table record has a mandatory relation to a package (the AD_Package). Choose a sensible package fitting to the functional area to which the table applies (so not the Core package). If no such package exist then create a new one. The relation to the module is maintained through the AD_Package, so an AD_Table has an AD_Package which belongs to a module. AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The timeout is the frequency (in seconds) which the ping for a cluster service is done, i.e., it represents the amount of time that should pass for the cluster node in charge of a cluster service to reaffirm itself as the leader. It is also used as a reference for the rest of the nodes in the cluster to determine if the leader is no longer alive and therefore if a new node should be promoted as the leader of the cluster service. Please note that it will be required to restart all the nodes in the cluster if this value is changed in order to make the new value visible for the entire cluster.

The rest of the records (the ones which do not comply with the whereclause) will be ignored both in export.database and update.database. AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

If the document is not saved, the preliminary number is displayed in "<>". AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. AD_FIELD.NAME: Concurrent Users Average
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Average number of concurrent users during last 30 days
AD_FIELD.HELP: Average number of concurrent users during last 30 days

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.HELP: The General Ledger Journal Batch identifies a group of journals to be processed as a group.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Key
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A fast method for finding a particular record.
AD_FIELD.HELP:
A search key allows for a fast method of finding a particular record. If you leave the search key empty, the system automatically creates a numeric number originating from a document sequence defined in the "Document Sequence" window. The sequence naming convention follows a rule "DocumentNo_TableName", where TableName is the actual name of the database table (e.g. C_Order).
Usually, company's internal identifiers for various records (products, customers, etc) are stored here.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Work Effort Incidence
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates each incidence of a work effort.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The time the process execution finished.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Product Revenue Return
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An account number in the general ledger to mark returns of this product.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Product Revenue Return Account indicates the account used for recording returns of this product.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Operative Quantity
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The number of a certain item involved in the transaction, according to the defined Operative UOM.

AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The amount debited from the account, given in provider currency.

AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the quantity of product needed to process one time the sequence.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Description

AD_FIELD.HELP: A description is limited to 255 characters.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Sales Campaign
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An advertising effort aimed at increasing sales.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Campaign defines a unique marketing program. Projects can be associated with a pre defined Marketing Campaign. You can then report based on a specific Campaign.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Conversion Rate
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Defines the conversion between Quantity and Process Quantity
AD_FIELD.HELP:
Defines how many final products each run of a process plan produces. See the following formula to understand the relation between the three elements:
Process Quantity = Quantity x Conversion Rate
